reason: Haematologic and immune dysfunction define hereditary HLH. Supplied HPO frequencies support direct hepatic and renal dysfunction at 30-79%; other findings do not justify displacing these within the cap.
Pancolitis is immune-mediated ulcerative inflammation of the entire colon, supporting gastrointestinal and infectious_immune primary axes.

Callosal dysgenesis defines neurologic disease. Reported skeletal abnormalities, strabismus and enteric aganglionosis meet the frequency threshold, although the two-patient evidence warrants medium confidence.

Neurodevelopmental impairment defines the syndrome. Restrictive ankyloglossia with frequent feeding difficulty supports gastrointestinal involvement; ptosis affects eyelids in 2/5. Small samples warrant medium confidence.
Food allergy is immune-mediated. Transient skin eruptions, gastrointestinal symptoms and episodic shock do not establish additional organ damage under the exclusion rules.
The tumour arises in cardiac muscle, establishing cardiovascular origin. The skeletal-muscle axis of the broader rhabdomyoma parent does not apply to this cardiac subtype.
Neurodevelopmental and skeletal abnormalities support the primary axes; congenital heart defects occur in roughly 40% of reported mosaic cases. Variable expression warrants medium confidence.
The defining mechanism is autoinflammatory. The predominant AGS presentation supports neurologic involvement; connective-tissue ancestry alone does not establish musculoskeletal damage.
Infection occupies orbital tissues, supporting ocular and infectious_immune primary axes. Skin involvement is not defining; an adjacent sinus infection is a separate source disease.

Cutaneous ossification progressing into muscle and fascia defines dermatologic and musculoskeletal disease. Endocrine dysfunction is neither defining nor sufficiently common; GNAS ancestry alone does not justify it.
